title: Fatimid Egyptian Caliphate
capsule: An Ismaili Shia caliphate ruling from Cairo, which it founded in 969. At its height it controlled Egypt, the Levant, and the holy cities; in this window it declined under military strongmen until Saladin abolished it in 1171, returning Egypt to Sunni allegiance.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases (Times Atlas of World History; Kinder & Hilgemann; Shepherd 1926) at ~0.07° resolution. Egyptian core well attested; authority over Syria and the Hijaz was often nominal or contested with local dynasts — treat eastern extents as claims. Confidence: high for Egypt, low–moderate for the Levant.
